title: Make the reconciliation report count only shards that finished

blocks.text: The nightly reconciliation splits the ledger into shards and matches each shard on a thread of its own. Finance wants the report at 06:00 whatever happens, so the job has a budget: when it runs out, the report goes out with whatever has finished. Twice this month the report's total matched no rerun of the same night, and once the job sat waiting on one stuck shard until an operator killed it.
`ShardReport.run(...)` already starts the shards; each one adds its matched amounts to its own slot of a plain `long[]`. Finish `collect(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ShardReport.java`.

When you're done, the report is ready by the deadline even if a shard is stuck, it totals the subtotals of the shards that finished, and it lists by index every shard that hadn't, counting nothing from them. Keep the subtotals in the plain array. About seven lines in total.
The tests hold some shards partway through their work until the test is over.

cases.says: when every shard finishes within the budget, the report totals all their subtotals and lists none as unfinished
a shard still running at the deadline is listed as unfinished, and none of the amounts it had matched so far is counted
with no budget left, the report is produced at once and lists every shard still running
a shard that never finishes doesn't hold the report past its budget

origin.section: A Read Is Guaranteed to See a Write Only If the Write Happens-Before It

concepts: A thread's writes happen-before another thread's return from join only when the join returns because the thread ended; a join that timed out gives no edge.
A read is guaranteed to see another thread's write only if the write happens-before it; without an edge the read is a data race and may return an older value.
